question: Which of the following insects has a pigment called ‘luciferin’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Firefly.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A pigment called luciferin is found in firefly.**
 
• Luciferin is a** light-emitting compound that is found in organisms that generate bioluminescence.**
 
• Luciferins typically undergo an enzyme-catalyzed reaction with molecular oxygen.
 
• They mix oxygen with this** pigment to generate light and a little heat.**
 
• Fireflies are also known as lightening bugs or winged beetles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Firefly:**

 
 
• Inside special cells, they combine oxygen with a substance called luciferin to make light with almost no heat.
 
• They use this light, called bioluminescence, to light up the ends of their abdomen.
 
• Each firefly species has its own unique flashing pattern.
